clue.text: Firm in which training is given priority?

definitions.meaning: firm in the sense of steady and secure

definitions.text: in which training is given priority?
definitions.meaning: a racing yard where horses are trained comes first, as its whole business

explanation.definitionFit: Firm and steady both mean secure; a racehorse trainer's yard is where training is the main business.

clue.text: Fascinated by army range

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Someone entranced by a military firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken with something is to be charmed or captivated by it.

clue.text: Broad line possibly made by shoulder-belt

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged in some other order to make a new word

explanation.surface: A thick stripe that might be produced by a strap worn over the shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of BROAD LINE; 'made by' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a belt slung across the shoulder and chest with loops for cartridges.

clue.text: English side supported by hooligan was eliminated

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits beneath, so it follows

parts.note: a side in cricket or football is a team of eleven, XI
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth often seen as a hooligan

explanation.surface: An English team backed by a thug got knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts TED underneath E and XI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exited a competition is to have left it, knocked out.

clue.text: Young seafarer unforthcoming about quantity of wine sailor's carrying

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the rest

parts.note: coy means shy and reluctant to give information

indicators.note: carrying says the sailor holds the next piece inside

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; the 's stands for 'has'
a bin is a stack or store of bottled wine

explanation.surface: A reticent young sailor whose shipmate smuggles a stack of wine aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unforthcoming' looks like a description of the boy but supplies the outer letters; 'sailor's carrying' reads 'sailor has carrying', so the sailor holds the wine store inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin boy is a lad serving as an attendant on a ship.

clue.text: Dressers having underwear entrusted to them?

definitions.text: Dressers having underwear entrusted to them?

parts.words: Dressers having underwear entrusted to them?
parts.note: dressers are bedroom furniture and drawers are also knickers, so the furniture is literally given underwear to keep

explanation.definitionFit: Bedroom furniture with sliding compartments is called a dresser, and its compartments share a name with knickers.

clue.text: Station dance is something of a game

parts.note: a base is a military or operational station
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A dance held at a station counts as a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is an American bat-and-ball sport, so it is a kind of game.

clue.text: Plutocrat returning from abroad turned up in British resort

annotationWithheld.why: Plutocrat returning from abroad turned up in British resort (5): 'Plutocrat returning from abroad' defines NABOB, but no reading of 'turned up in British resort' builds NABOB or its reverse BOBAN; the resort's name seems lost from the clue as held

clue.text: Not fit to watch anything but black-and-white films?

definitions.meaning: not fit means unwell, a little poorly

definitions.text: to watch anything but black-and-white films?
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone who prefers films that are not in colour

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill is being unwell; read literally the phrase also describes films lacking colour.

clue.text: Runner initially noticing several people engaged in watersports

parts.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: divers is an old word meaning several or sundry

explanation.surface: An athlete first spots a group of swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but it is SKI; 'divers' in the old sense of 'various' gives the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers who go underwater with goggles and flippers take part in a sport in water.

clue.text: Polish fellow regarded as an expert

definitions.meaning: polish means rub a surface to make it shine
an enthusiast who knows a great deal about a subject

explanation.definitionFit: To polish leather is to rub it bright; an enthusiast with deep knowledge, like a film fan, is also called this.

clue.text: Popular party fast becoming lackadaisical

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a do is a party or celebration
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A well-liked celebration turns into a lazy fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackadaisical and lazy both describe someone without energy or effort.

clue.text: Primate's embargo receiving loud expression of disapproval

indicators.note: receiving means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a ban is an embargo or prohibition
boo is what a crowd shouts in disapproval

explanation.surface: A primate's prohibition is met with jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large African monkey, and monkeys belong to the primates.

clue.text: Old priests seen in Morocco by serviceman

parts.note: MA is the international vehicle code for Morocco
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Ancient clerics are spotted in North Africa beside a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the priestly caste of ancient Persia, like the wise men of the Nativity.

clue.text: Instrument producing very high notes?

parts.note: high here means up a mountain: the horn is played in the Alps rather than at a high pitch

explanation.definitionFit: This long wooden horn is blown by herders in the Swiss mountains, so its notes sound at great altitude.

clue.text: Offering to repair boot withnail

indicators.note: to repair means to put right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A gift for mending a boot along with a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' signals an anagram of BOOT and NAIL; 'with' joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a gift presented to God, a religious offering.

clue.text: Spinner's trajectory described as excellent

definitions.meaning: the path through the air of a spinning top, a toy

explanation.definitionFit: First-rate sports teams play in the leading division; read literally it is the flight of a spinning toy.

clue.text: Incomer evoking strong resentment

parts.note: str is a dictionary abbreviation for strong, as in grammar's strong verbs
anger is resentment or indignation

explanation.surface: A newcomer arouses bitter feeling among locals.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is a newcomer from elsewhere, someone unfamiliar to the locals.

clue.text: Kidnapped is full of vigour

explanation.definitionFit: Someone whisked off in secret has been spirited away; a lively, energetic person is also so described.

clue.text: A few lines in Arabic penned by secretary

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in a pen

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A short passage written in Arabic by an office assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a short section of text, a few lines long.

clue.text: Celt getting excited about very big secret

indicators.note: about means the scrambled word goes round the next piece
getting excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A Celtic person is thrilled by a huge secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting excited' rearranges the four letters of 'Celt'; 'about' then wraps that scramble round OS, the clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means hidden or private, as in a closet fan.

clue.text: A new board game artist made from expensive material

parts.note: Go is an ancient Asian board game of stones
RA is a Royal Academician, a British artist

explanation.surface: A board game made by an artist from luxurious fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is soft, costly wool from a rabbit or goat, a luxurious textile.

clue.text: Progressive lacking power?

parts.note: something moving forward without an engine of its own, because it is being pulled by another vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A broken-down car pulled behind a truck moves forward without using its own engine.

clue.text: Signal many waited for when left in a cellar, maybe?

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other words before they are mixed
maybe says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: During an air raid, people sheltering in a cellar wait for the siren to say it is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L among A CELLAR, and 'maybe' signals an anagram of the whole eight letters; the surface is the wartime raid shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: After a wartime air raid a siren sounded to say the danger was over.

clue.text: Cancel arrangement for girl to come over mid-July

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that comes over sits above the next

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: mid means take the middle letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Calling off a plan for a girl to visit in the middle of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-July' gives UL, the middle letters of JULY, and 'to come over' sets ANN above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, to revoke it.

clue.text: After a job

definitions.meaning: a prefix meaning after, as in postwar

explanation.definitionFit: The prefix in postwar means later than; a position in a firm is also called by this word.

clue.text: Bribe professional killers to supply means of silencing squeakers?

parts.note: to grease someone's palm is to bribe them
guns is slang for hired gunmen

explanation.surface: Paying off hitmen to provide a way of silencing informers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeakers' reads as informers to be silenced by killers, but it means squeaking hinges and machinery quieted with lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool for forcing lubricant into bearings stops machinery creaking and squealing.

clue.text: Girl takes merchandise inadvertently

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
wares are goods for sale

explanation.surface: A girl walks off with goods without meaning to.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught unawares means taken by surprise, without knowing or intending.

clue.text: Extract from Clement Attlee's talk

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage taken from a speech by the post-war British Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Britain's Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951; the run starts at the last letter of Clement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle chatter or gossip, a kind of talk.
